clips.scene: A medieval European army assembling on a churned, overcast battlefield near Legnica, Poland, April 9, 1241 — dozens of soldiers with kite shields and spears, banners whipping violently in the wind, horses breathing hard nearby, real individual motion throughout (no static crowd). HAZEL walks forward through the ranks facing the lens, urgent, delivering her FULL line uninterrupted. The INSTANT she finishes speaking, a war horn suddenly sounds — she turns sharply, the view swinging past her own shoulder toward the horizon; the shot ENDS on her alarmed profile as she registers that something is there, before anything on the horizon is clearly visible yet (the reveal itself is the NEXT clip, not this one).
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (breathless, urgent, to lens, COMPLETE sentence, not cut off): "April, 1241. Europe is about to face the Mongols."
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. She is walking the entire time, never planted/static. She delivers her full line clearly and completely — do NOT cut off or interrupt her dialogue. The horn sounds right as she finishes the line (interrupting the moment/beat afterward, not her speech), and she turns sharply in reaction to it. End the shot on her alarmed/startled expression looking toward the horizon, NOT on a resolved view of the Mongol army — that reveal belongs to the next clip.
clips.sound: Wind, banners snapping, horses breathing and shifting, distant murmur of the assembling army, then a SUDDEN loud war horn right as she finishes speaking

clips.scene: Continuous from clip 1's exact moment and location: HAZEL is still facing the horizon, facing the lens. In the FIRST half of the shot, dust is thinning enough to reveal a nearer, smaller cluster of individual Mongol horsemen at the edge of visibility — each one distinct: different poses, individually visible composite bows, lamellar/leather armor, horse tack, a banner — NOT a uniform blurred mass or repeated identical silhouette. In the SECOND half of the shot, the camera/her attention pulls back or the dust continues clearing to reveal the FULL scale: thousands more Mongol cavalry stretching across the horizon in organized formations, dust rising behind them. The escalation from 'a identifiable handful of riders' to 'the full horde' happens live, within this one continuous take.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (breathless, reacting in the same instant she sees each layer of it — first the near riders, then the full scale; "Mongols" is already named in clip 1's complete line, so this is a pure in-the-moment reaction, not a repeat of the name): "...oh my god. They're actually here." [beat, as the full scale becomes visible] "I need to find whoever's in charge." [already turning/moving toward the army's command group as she says this — bridges into clip 2]
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. Her dialogue is reactive and paced to what she is seeing AT THAT MOMENT, not stated calmly in advance — the first line lands as the near riders resolve into focus, the second line lands as the full horizon-wide scale becomes visible, and by the end of the line she is already turning her body away from the horizon toward camp (motion that clip 2 continues, not a fresh static start). Do not render the cavalry as a flat, repeated, or synthetic-looking silhouette — individual riders and horses must read as distinct photographed subjects even at a distance (varied poses, realistic overlapping, natural spacing, not a copy-pasted texture).
clips.sound: The war horn's echo fading, then a rising rumble of thousands of hooves, distant Mongol horns answering, wind carrying dust

clips.scene: Opens continuing the exact turning motion clip 1B ended on (motion continuation, not a fresh static start) — HAZEL arrives at Duke Henry II the Pious, mounted on his horse, nobles and soldiers around him, facing the lens the whole time with Henry visible over her shoulder/beside her in the same frame (never a separate reverse shot of him alone).
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (arriving, still completing the turn/approach from 1B): "Duke Henry the Second. He's leading them." HAZEL (to Henry, still facing the lens): "How many are we fighting?" [Henry] (grim, eyes on the horizon, visible in her frame): "Enough." [beat — Mongol cavalry begins moving in the background, visible over his shoulder in her shot] [Henry] (shouted — this exact line and the cavalry motion behind him are the bridge into clip 3, not a fresh unrelated start): "Hold the line!"
clips.action: Henry looks to the horizon BEFORE he answers — the look precedes the line, not after. He raises his weapon and calls to his own line only after Mongol movement is already visible behind him in the same continuous take. Single continuous unbroken shot, no cuts. End the shot with his shout and the cavalry's motion still building, ready to be picked up and closed to full gallop at the very start of clip 3.
clips.sound: Wind, restless horses, low murmur of nobles, Henry's voice grim and commanding, distant horns beginning on the Mongol side
